reviews.text: Some may find the ending acceptable but unfortunately it hurt the film considerably for me.
reviews.author: Nyle Coleman

reviews.text: It falters when it comes to action, especially during a climax that takes place in the middle of a storm, and where the violence becomes murky and hard to enjoy. “The Equalizer 2” never reaches the same level as its predecessor. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Denzel is always immensely watchable and the hurricane-set finale is packed with suspense, but overall the movie is dampened by an unfocused and predictable plot.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Those random bits of setup that are thrown into the early parts of the film feel almost entirely gratuitous and do nothing but distract from what’s going on around them, but they actually get far more irritating once they start to pay off.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: Washington is such a joy to watch. The seasoned star hasn’t lost a bit of his allure, and his ability to carry a film is unmatched.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: This twisty sequel takes the temperature and weight of the cold lead hammer that is Denzel and heats it with anger and stakes to match the hot lead being shot around him.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 leaves the viewer with a boredom hangover - a cloudy funk that lingers well after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A step up from the original, raising the stakes and making an effort that's not just watchable, it's occasionally even enjoyable.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: An enjoyable action-packed film with terrific pacing; the two-hour runtime flies right on by.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: A solidly entertaining popcorn flick with pretensions of bringing Shakespearean level of pathos to the tale of vengeance.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 is another blockbuster to join all the other summer sequels in box office heaven.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: The revelations are entirely predictable and the assemblage of villains serve only as fodder for ruthless slaughtering.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: I can't tell you to pay $12 dollars to see this movie, not with all the other goods currently in theaters.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: A better film because Denzel's in it.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 lectures its audience about the importance of life itself -- and then pulls a gun on whatever importance might exist.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Fuqua and company trade in the vicious streak that made the first film so gleefully mean for ho-hum tedium.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: There are probably one or two too many subplots that don't really amount to much, but any excuse to see this actor try on different hats as the same character is pretty exciting. This is a mild recommendation.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Fuqua's direction is slick but generally uninspired.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: This might not be a great piece of awards-bait filmmaking but it is a rather enjoyable movie.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: While not reinventing the wheel of modern-day action thrillers, if viewers liked the first film, this new outing may provide similar feelings once the end credits roll.
reviews.author: Devvon Eubanks

reviews.text: And through it all, the noise and the quiet, [Denzel] Washington dominates, even surrounded by a group of terrific supporting players.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Not bad, but why does Denzel make a transition in the first movie to this one from a once hardened military soldier into a disheveled dopey guy that likely doesn't know how to comb his hair? It just started to go in a weird direction.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: The Equalizer was a satisfying action yarn, but this sequel offers few similar pleasures.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A remarkable thriller that I've personally enjoyed more than its predecessor. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A film with characters that we care about, a spectacular, violent and intelligently action, and an impeccable Denzel Washington. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Washington's first sequel is likely to be remembered for that trivia nugget and almost nothing else. It's the kind of movie so confused that Ta-Nehisi Coates' work is repeatedly name checked but the film also stops for a respectability politics lecture.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: One can't help but feel that The Equaliser 2 could have exploited the taxi driver set-up in a more intense manner akin to Collateral.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: A sequel only in name and not by nature, The Equalizer 2 doesn't differentiate itself from any number of the countless male-driven action projects doing the rounds these days
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Yes, the plot is very much B-movie fare, but the star brings his A-game.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: There have been several Denzel Washington films over the years that were worthy of sequels and the seasoned actor surely considered the merits of each one. That's what makes his choice of the utterly disposable The Equalizer 2 such a mystery.
reviews.author: Julie Crawford

reviews.text: If you're a fan of Washington as a general rule, you shouldn't be dissatisfied with his portrayal - instead, you can reserve your disappointment for the film's slow pacing and uninspired action beats.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: While the movie might not be great, it's extremely watchable thanks to the inescapable charismatic magnetism of its star.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: If you're a fan of Denzel Washington then I think we can all agree that this movie is just padding his stats at this point.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Between the moralizing life lessons that are spouted at full volume intensity, the film doesn't shy away from graphic, bloody violence.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 begins with a lot of momentum. It dissipates as attention shifts to Washington's former spy colleagues.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: [Denzel] Washington doesn't bring anything novel to his acting tool belt, yet it has enough focus to become a successful B-movie, even if it is weirdly preachy.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is cut from the same cloth as one and packs in quite a few punches. It's a delight for action seekers and diehard Washington fans - there's plenty of both to 'equalize' the obvious flaws.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: A bad sequel to a mediocre previous installment. Who could've predicted this?
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 ultimately joins other conveyor belt revenge fantasies haphazardly conceived in 2018...
reviews.author: Frank Ochieng

reviews.text: A vengeful Denzel is a sight to behold and I root for this franchise's existence but it seems like it's too much to ask for the movies themselves to live up to the standard of their star.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Fun in the moment, but forgettable after, Fuqua and Washington's sequel is a passable revenge thriller.
reviews.author: Cameron Frew

reviews.text: Even with a relatively weak plot, Washington demonstrates flashes of bloody excitement as he dispatches armed goons in steady intervals...That said, my audience reacted even more during the dramatic moments, graced by his Final Form as Uncle Denzel.
reviews.author: VyceVictus

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 creates a fantasy world in which issues are black and white, and one man can control the destiny of those around him by sheer force of will. It's a staple in Antoine Fuqua and Denzel Washington's collaborations
reviews.author: Ed Travis

reviews.text: Fuqua's movie, unqualified to create anything other than superficial poignancy, is empty, tiresome and uninteresting...
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: Because it stars Washington and is directed by Antoine Fuqua, it's going to have much more competence and sheen than comparable genre fare.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The blandness of "Equalizer 2" even extends to Washington himself. This is the closest he's come to sleepwalking through a role.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: An entertaining sequel that packs more power with each punch.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Sure, praise is granted for some well choreographed slayings, but considering the cost of a movie ticket today, you're better off staying home and waiting for this one on basic cable.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Another nasty, bone dry revenge thriller in which the coming storm of Washington's wrath is literalised as an on screen weather event.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Despite its glossy sheen, this is just run-of-the-mill pulp fiction.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Watch the film for its superbly executed action and for more of a story than the last one. And for the behemoth called Denzel Washington...
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: It is blunt, humourless and brutal, and reminds of the no-nonsense action films of the 1970s and early 1980s.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: Denzel is Denzel, and he's going to deliver every time.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: The early action scenes on their own have a classic, macho rhythm. But you can't just write a tough guy, you need to give him a place to go.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: A disjointed plot, cliched characters, casting that pretty much works as a spoiler, and the clunkiest of visual metaphors - it is a mess, and a dull one at that.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Washington is a pleasure to watch on the screen. The two-time Oscar winner is able to tap into his own surplus of moral righteousness even when the script is pulling the carpet out from under him.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: I honestly felt like the first half of this was better than the first [movie].
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: Everything in the movie is ridiculous... I'm waiting for the third one and he's working for Domino's.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is more than a worthwhile proposal. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Dull, pretentious, and mostly disposable.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The best moments of Equalizer 2 are wasted in a film that confuses personality with pretension, in a story too frivolous to deserve the talent that has set it. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: It's often cheesy and it's not deep, despite repeated cameos for a copy of Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time, but it is, appropriately enough, the equal of The Equalizer.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The confused, meandering course makes this difficult to get behind, while its idea of a climax is a CGI hurricane.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is no improvement on the 2014 movie.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: In summary, it is a good product, which questions and interrogates while it houses a franchise that is somewhat uncomfortable to place in the contemporary mainstream panorama. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Tejero Nogales

reviews.text: Fuqua delivers a very reserved product, without being risky both in the plot and in its development, and this ends up taking its toll. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Rosales Santos

reviews.text: Clunky, over-processed cement-mixer cinema, given some consistency by Washington's screen presence...
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: There are things to enjoy.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Fuqua and Washington manage to deliver a strong ending, but the energy wasted on the way makes for a baggy film.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: It has a one-of-a-kind star front and centre and in allowing him to do his thing, we get a sequel that's uncommonly worthwhile.
reviews.author: Ross Miller

reviews.text: ... if anyone can make meaningless look meaningful, it's Denzel. That's a big energy.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: A thriller that is sustained by a renowned actor accompanied by a solid cast that, although lost among small stories, ultimately comes out ahead as the action tape he promised to be. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: A bloated, confusing, and terribly bland thriller.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: It's ridiculous, of course. And it's violent. It's also impeccably executed (pun intended), powerfully acted and sincerely acknowledges the value of goodness, virtue and doing the right thing.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: A tense crowdpleaser, but no one is stretching here, including the viewer.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: This is far more rhythmically assured than the first one, and gains a feel for urban melancholy in the editing and score that nudges close to elegance at times.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: A film of such frustrating ineptitude it doesn't even deserve the "Sequelizer" pun some critics have been applying to it.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 is a guilty pleasure - a by-the-numbers sequel given extra impetus by the presence of one of Hollywood's finest leading men.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: It's purely designed to be a high-intensity, exploitative bloodbath, and it does that very well.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: It's a struggle to work out the point of the film.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: It's the same action-and-avenging nonsense as before, but directed with fair zest by Antoine Fuqua.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Denzel Washington's in rattling form. But when is he ever not?
reviews.author: John Byrne

reviews.text: More of the same from this franchise please.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: A marked improvement over its predecessor, packing in a handful of moments of legitimately spine-straightening suspense and, thank goodness, a sense of purpose for its lead.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: After four films with Fuqua, it's time for [Washington] to find a collaborator interested in making something more challenging than these childish, retrograde, wish fulfillment fantasies.
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: It's about as enjoyable as the first...there are some really good sequences with terrific dialogue. Plotting is the biggest issue here.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: The character in question, The Equalizer, shares the peaceful job of taxi driver with that of the relentless avenger of injustice and innocent victims... a sign of the film's lack of narrative continuity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Francisco Marinero

reviews.text: Once it's over, you won't necessarily be itching for an Equalizer 3.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: What makes The Equalizer 2as engaging as it is, is that we care for these characters in a way that most action movies tend to ignore.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: The most notable thing about Equalizer 2 is the stylistic force of its director in the execution of its action scenes that take us to the darkest corners of the protagonist's soul. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcos Gandía

reviews.text: The Equalizer (2014) was one of those films that almost everyone forgot after seeing it, but that so many people saw that a sequel was already justified. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is much more than a showcase vehicle for Washington. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: Fragmented with too many subplots and unnecessarily sadistic violence, it's a ponderously contrived, avenging hero melodrama...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The tired, slow-burn movie around [Washington] ... is almost as punishing to an audience as McCall is to his prey.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Having McCall take a part-time gig as a Lyft driver hardly qualifies as meaningful character development - it's hardly even a useful plot device.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The Equalizer films don't exactly push him beyond his comfort zone. But they celebrate the icon that Denzel is. They play on his persona, they savour his looming presence, and they give him more to chew on than similar films would.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: A solid, value-driven action thriller...The magnificently tense finale, which takes place in an evacuated coastal town about to be torn apart by a hurricane has so many religious references it's hard to keep count.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 is only the second in a series that already feels as if it is riddled with sequel fatigue.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: Unless Fuqua settles the vibranium question and tones the violence down, I'd prefer they don't team up for a third one.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Essentially, if your idea of a good night out is watching Denzel Washington hang tough and destroy deserving scumbags, there's something for you here.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: It's just very standard, very predictable, very much exactly the movie you think it's going to be: that is the whole of its appeal and also its most glaring limitation.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: It's worth checking out, although on cable.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: It's not much of a movie - more a parade of rah-rah triumphs obscuring a batch of logical oddities - which makes Washington's committed performance stand out like the heavenly host in the night sky over Bethlehem.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Washington's implacable charisma and Fuqua's robust command of pace and style are desperately needed because writer Robert Wenk is back too, and he's flat out of ideas.
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is an entertaining time at the movies, but if they had only insisted on closing the plot holes and making a vivid villain, it could have been an outright classic.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: McCall, for all his high-minded talk, seems to take a little too much sick glee in all the bloodletting he engages in.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: In the end, we have very good action sequences adorned with unnecessary well-intentioned speeches imposed upon them. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: It's something of a snoozer, featuring a low-energy performance by Denzel, who spends much of the film quietly observing and very little time delivering impassioned speeches or putting inferior people into their place.
reviews.author: Dustin Rowles

reviews.text: A couple of hours of pseudo-thoughtful entertainment.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It tries to be a thoughtful action thriller, but ultimately feels like a charade. It looks ponderous, but really there's nothing there.
reviews.author: Damian Levy

reviews.text: The pacing of the film may be brisk, and the action scenes energizing, but a close look at the fight choreography shows that it concise and calculating.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: McCall is tailor-made for Washington, who plays AARP cool, yet deadly, better than anyone.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Washington's McCall is a compelling character, the kind you'd quite happily like to hang out with whether he's busting heads or painting walls.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt (UK)

reviews.text: Equalizer 2 is a slow, ponderous affair that not even Denzel's considerable charisma can save.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Despite the implausibility and the troubling violence that Fuqua always forces on his audience, it is an entertaining film.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: This sequel to The Equalizer, itself based on the 1980s TV series, is more of the same, with (too) familiar screenwriting, a compelling lead character, and inventive action scenes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Even with Washington at the top of his game, "The Equalizer 2" just doesn't deliver the thrills.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Denzel Washington may be over 60 but as his work in his first sequel ever here proves he is definitely not over the hill.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: We've already mentioned that "Equalizer 2" offers more of the same, with its main attraction still giving his all while looking as if every vigilante move comes so very, very easily. That likely will be good enough for loyal Denzel fans of all ages.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: How do the filmmakers settle on a narrative for an Equalizer film? The answer is they don't, cramming several plotlines into one jumbled film.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Standard-issue crime-drama stuff, but Fuqua gives it the aura and gravity of a much more important movie.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Denzel Washington's The Equalizer 2, a pointlessly violent sequel to his pointlessly brutal 2014 box-office success, confirms the pointlessly dangerous black-male stereotype that sells.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Everything that's wrong with the modern summer blockbuster: a meaningless franchise with only star power in its favor.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: There is a tonal consistency to The Equalizer II its predecessor never had.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The film would have collapsed into a mess with a lesser actor in the starring role. Washington manages to keep the film interesting even when the story takes on such an uninspired direction.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: This is a thought-provoking thriller.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: The character remains strong. The script, not so much.
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: I'm not sure audiences are getting what they deserve with this plodding, so-so action-thriller, but they'll get what they'll pay for...
reviews.author: Brad Wheeler

reviews.text: A less-muddled script could have rescued "The Equalizer 2" from the summer blahs, but as it is, we'll just have to accept it for its strengths while acknowledging its flaws.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Less attention has been paid to Richard Wenk's screenplay, a contrived work that traffics in lapses of common sense and internal logic, plus an artificially sweet ending.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: The film never jells. The main villains are cookie-cutter archetypes. No effort is made to give them any depth or personality.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: It felt like a season of television crushed into two hours.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Pretty much the same style as the original but a little better. That's mostly due to Denzel's chemistry with the kid played by Ashton Sanders.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Denzel Washington and Ashton Sanders of Moonlight bring nice father-son chemistry to violent action film.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Denzel continues to have the time of his life being this solitary avenging angel, and Fuqua is painting every moment of extreme violence dark crimson.
reviews.author: Jacob Knight

reviews.text: Anchored by Denzel Washington's steely presence, it's a spare, brutal vigilante exercise, with an element of righteous revenge mixed into the balance.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: McCall's moral compass is in short supply these days...
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: This is an action movie in which the action star strives to be, well, inactive.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Denzel returns to lay on rough, R-rated justice. Yeah, the two-time Oscar winner is punching below his weight in a vigilante movie. But nothing dims his star power. Nothing.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Washington brings nuance to an otherwise black-and-white scenario, which elevates The Equalizer 2 above so many other "nice guy/secret killer" films.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: Wenk may have stuffed one too many plotlines into McCall's return, the resulting film often feeling disjointed, its central crime more MacGuffin than mystery to be solved.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Denzel Washington is superbly watchable, as always, but Antoine Fuqua's sequel to his (not quite) everyman hero story swaps smarts and arty aspirations for mindless violence.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: This follow-up is many things, and often chaotically tries to combine them all at once.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: By the time the film concludes, I'm hoping Washington and Fuqua are willing to make a second exception to release a third installment.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Suggests intriguing questions about the moral and ethical imperatives of justice...answers these questions with an Old Testament zeal: evil must be smitten by self-appointed good men.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: This time around, Denzel's "Equalizer" is less of a Robin Hood-like hero for the helpless, and more of a Travis Bickle-like vigilante, shooting his way through a murder caper.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Though it boasts some cool action scenes and a strong central performance, the movie is weighed down by a muddled script and bland storytelling efforts.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Robert McCall may have been better suited to an age when you could channel-hop to Spenser: For Hire or Remington Steele... As a multiplex offering, alongside tiny superheroes and giant dinosaurs, he may not be worth your time, even every four years.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: A reasonably well-written and (of course) beautifully acted serving of geriatric-virility violence porn...
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: The action turns out even shoddier in this second outing, particularly during a climactic blowout on an island hit by a hurricane. That may sound exciting on paper, but not when the winds render the dust-up barely visible.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: "The Equalizer" should be locked in a room with "The Terminator." Then this lousy series would finally be killed off.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: For a supposed action film, The Equalizer 2 is a slow burner, giving Washington the chance to prove as an actor he's a master of his domain in his own right.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The elements of the original film that felt tacked on or out of character have been emphasized in The Equalizer 2.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Gory and silly.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: [It] won't be considered a standout in the career of the director or the actor, but it's not an embarrassment either.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: The film's slow-burn approach matches that of the original. Fuqua is in no hurry and understands that building a story gradually pays dividends later in the proceedings.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The film is effective where it needs to be, and if there is an "Equalizer 3," in line to see it is where you'll find me.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: The worst movie of Denzel Washington's career.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: With the secret behind his formidable skills out of the bag, all we have is a good guy who is good at things, and a sense of obligation to conjure up a convoluted syndicate of straw men for him to chop down.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: The moral of the story in Equalizer 2 is that if you don't find yourself on Robert McCall's bad side, you're likely to be okay.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The film manages to create a perfect balance between the codes of an emotional drama and an action film.
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: He's never referred to as "the Equalizer" by those around him, but he might as well be, given that he's just a cape away from being a full-fledged superhero.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: In a genre that too often descends into unthinking sadism and stereotyping, The Equalizer 2 exceeded my expectations...
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Like all great actors, Mr. Washington commits to the performance, but every so often he also breathes fire, imbuing a scene with such shocking ferocity and bone-deep moral certitude that everything else falls blissfully away.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It's a well-executed popcorn flick with some feeling, and better than the first. I wouldn't even mind a third.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Betrayal, loss, grief, redemption - it's the stuff great characters are built on. And it makes all those thrilling knife fights and broken bones actually mean something.
reviews.author: Barbara VanDenburgh

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 tries way too hard to play the action sequences straight.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: Fuqua has made sure this follow-up is more of the same, playing it oddly safe with material that doesn't do particularly well with complete darkness.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Straight-forward, bone-crunching, nonsense, Antoine Fuqua's "Death Wish" like revenge tale is an unapologetic crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It's gritty, dramatic, powerful and tense. There is a satisfying pay off and Washington is as good as ever. However, the film has lost much of what made it unique.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: A narratively and visually muddled disappointment, one that regularly confuses numbing brutality with vicariously thrilling righteous vengeance.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: A preposterous and pedestrian action-thriller.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A movie that's watchable and intermittently pleasing. But not enough time was spent getting the substance right.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: We think of the Equalizer films as action movies, but there's really not a ton of action. Often what we get - and like - is McCall as life coach.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: By sequelising The Equalizer, Denzel has given himself a franchise wherein he can consistently murder, monologue and moralise.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: "...builds on the low-flash action chops of the original to bring us more of the good stuff..."
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: There's not much effort to tie it all together with any kind of plausible, big-picture cohesion, but no matter. All we need to know is some very bad people have crossed Robert McCall, and that's almost always a deadly mistake.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 is symptomatic of a confused time when people are collectively looking for invulnerable superheroes who don't so much as speak truth to injustice as beat the hell out of it, and its cathartic pleasures leave a bad taste.
reviews.author: Niles Schwartz

reviews.text: Fuqua has always been adept at stirring a moody, anticipatory anxiety, at the anticipation of violence, but the buildup often proves more engaging onscreen than the actual onslaught.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: Even the most easily satisfied fans of Washington will be unlikely to find much of anything in this sadistic, stupid and sloppy sequel.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Fuqua and Washington have developed a body of work over the years that is, if nothing else, reliably kinetic. But with Wenk's pedestrian writing, there just isn't much for Washington to work with here.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: It's got some curves and tension, but it's dogged by issues.
reviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 never comes close to the delicious highs of like-minded flicks like Taken or John Wick, but Fuqua does improve upon the sloppy, poorly lit squabbles of the original.
reviews.author: Randall Colburn

reviews.text: For a film whose hero prides himself on "equalizing" the playing field for those who cannot defend themselves, The Equalizer 2 is incredibly uneven.
reviews.author: Andrew Husband

reviews.text: Robert McCall is a great action hero, but all things being equalized, he deserves a better movie.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Worst of all, it leaves the door open for "The Equalizer 3."
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: It's hard to argue with McCall's mission, or his brutally crunchy methods. So why does it all feel so unoriginal and grim and dull?
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: Hiring Denzel to play him is a lot like paying Frank Gehry to design your doghouse: He'll get the job done, and probably do it really well, but surely his talents could be much better applied to almost any other task?
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: That Washington is charming enough to disguise McCall's clear streak of Travis Bickle-level sociopathy ranks as this production's greatest asset.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: There surely are some fantastic tales to tell with this character, and that potential still exists, but this really isn't one of them.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: This distinctive character is gradually subsumed by familiar genre imperatives that eventually make McCall seem less special and singular than he did on first exposure in 2014.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Judging by the ponderous tone and pace, Fuqua thinks he's making high art (likely aspiring to something existential like Jean-Pierre Melville's "Le Samouraï"), but this is a grisly exploitation movie at best.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: In the past, this kind of character, who abhors swear words but kills with obvious relish, would've been positioned as an interesting contrast. In The Equalizer 2 it just feels like unexamined orthodoxy.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Outside of the performance from Denzel Washington, which is obviously good, the only engaging dynamic here is Robert trying to set Miles on the right path. The Equalizer 2 is fairly boring whenever they aren't interacting together
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A satisfactory sequel, where Washington and Fuqua manage to improve upon the best qualities of the original. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Denzel crushes this role and turns a would-be straight-to-DVD movie into a legitimate slobberknocker!
reviews.author: Ja-Quan Greene

reviews.text: He's cool, with moral clarity and he's three moves ahead of everyone. No wonder he's such a welcome sight in 2018 America and no wonder Washington wanted another go-around.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Despite deeply flawed storytelling, it demonstrates how a great actor in a great role can turn an otherwise mediocre story into a satisfyingly visceral, cathartic thrill ride.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Denzel again delivers as a relentless killing machine eager to execute any evildoers dumb enough to cross his path!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Denzel Washington is excellent as McCall, and he brings out the best in Richard Wenk's script. If you are a fan of the original film, you will very likely appreciate this latest chapter.
reviews.author: JimmyO

reviews.text: Denzel Washington and Antoine Fuqua have created a unique Punisher-with-heart vigilante character that is a pleasant thrill to watch and a modest delight to revisit.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: I know why I shouldn't like The Equalizer 2, and yet I'd be thrilled if they ended up churning out a new Equalizer movie every few years.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: There's the old cliché that says, "so-and-so is such a great actor he could read the phone book (whatever that is; as I said, it's an old cliché) and make it interesting." That's pretty much what Washington pulls off in "EQ2."
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 is an equally stylish sequel to Antoine Fuqua and Denzel Washington's action drama, but with fewer thrills and surprises.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: It's an absurd opening that promises something glorious... Alas, this is not that movie.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: The Equalizer 2 tries hard to re-create that primal red-meat formula, but it takes far too long puttering around to really deliver the exploitation goods. Just get to the equalizing already!
reviews.author: Andrew Wright

reviews.text: No amount of Denzel Washington's weary authority is enough to distract from the fact that this overstuffed, ultimately unsatisfying potboiler merely dresses up its cliches in strained gravitas.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The climactic dispensation of rough justice... is almost worth the price of admission. However, the grind of the getting-there could have you requesting a discount.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The movie is a bog; Washington's merely wading through it.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: An unexpected but terrific character piece punctuated with thrilling action beats.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: This solid, but unspectacular sequel (Washington's first in a more than 50-film career) is a movie that plays by a "very particular set" of rules.
reviews.author: James Croot

synopsis: If you have a problem and there is nowhere else to turn, the mysterious and elusive Robert McCall will deliver the vigilante justice you seek. This time, however, McCall's past cuts especially close to home when thugs kill Susan Plummer -- his best friend and former colleague. Now out for revenge, McCall must take on a crew of highly trained assassins who'll stop at nothing to destroy him.
